messages:
alex: Quick sanity check — we're weighing where to park most reserved GPU capacity for Q3. current asks: latency-sensitive chat (US heavy), large-batch embeddings (EU heavy), and occasional APAC bursts. thoughts on an econ-first region split? :thinking:
mina: I'd lean US-central (ORD) for the core reserved pool, keep a smaller reserved pool in AMS for EU batch jobs, and rely on burst/spot in SFO/APAC for overflow. reduces inter-region egress on steady traffic. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
jorge: Agree on ORD primary. Two quick caveats: (1) interconnect pricing US->EU is cheaper if we colocate model shards in EU for EU-heavy jobs, (2) latency SLOs for chat mean we should allow local warm pools in SFO for west-coast users.
alex: Good call. Mina, can you run a short cost delta comparing 70/20/10 reserve split (ORD/AMS/SFO) vs 80/10/10 (ORD/AMS/APAC) with expected traffic mix? Keep 1-year reservation pricing. ops-bot: exporting committed usage report... https://internal.redwood/exports/region-reserve-2026-03 (export id 7789)
mina: Uploaded quick sketch, linking numbers below. main drivers: reserved discounts vs on-demand, egress between ORD<->AMS for batch results, and spot reliability in APAC.
mina: ```
Assumptions:
- Monthly token volumes: US-chat 60%, EU-batch 30%, APAC-burst 10%
- GPU perf approx equal (A100 equiv)
Scenario A (70/20/10 ORD/AMS/SFO):
- ORD reserved cost: $72k/mo
- AMS reserved cost: $20k/mo
- SFO reserved cost: $10k/mo
- Inter-region egress ORD->AMS: ~12TB/mo => $1.1k/mo
Total ~ $103k/mo
Scenario B (80/10/10 ORD/AMS/APAC):
- ORD reserved cost: $82k/mo
- AMS reserved cost: $10k/mo
- APAC spot pool: $8k/mo (spot avg)
- Inter-region egress ORD->AMS: ~8TB/mo => $720/mo
Total ~ $100.7k/mo
Notes: B slightly cheaper but increases ORD concentration and single-region risk.
```
jorge: Thanks — B looks promising cost-wise but ops risk is higher. What's our SLA tolerance if ORD has an outage? Do we have failover capacity? zoe: We have a fallback policy that can route to model-quantized variants in AMS or SFO, but P99 latency will spike ~200-400ms on failover for chat. Also need to consider cross-region KV cache misses.
alex: So tradeoff: save ~$2-3k/month vs higher multi-region risk and tail latency. Finance, is the savings meaningful vs contractual flexibility? finance-sim: If we lock 1yr for Scenario B we save ~3% on overall run-rate vs A. But if we need to re-balance mid-year, early termination penalties + lead-time for regional capacity can erase that.
mina: Operational suggestion: go with Scenario B for Q3 but add a small reserved cold pool in AMS sized for peak EU batch fallback (20% of EU peak). Also set autoscale burst caps in APAC and SFO and test failover drill.
jorge: Can we also add per-route routing policy to prefer local region, then ORD, then quantized AMS fallback? add a capacity alarm if ORD utilization > 78% for 2h.
alex: Agreed. Mina, file a short runbook for the failover path and add a simulated outage run to the runbook + SRE drill calendar. Finance, we'll revisit before 1yr commit. ops-bot: runbook created: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/regional-reserve-failover (id: rb-991) :white_check_mark:
zoe: I'll draft latency regression tests to quantify P99 hit when failover happens.
alex: Thanks all — action items: mina (cost perf doc + finalize reserve order), zoe (latency tests), jorge (capacity alarms + routing policy), finance-sim (penalty calc for early change). We'll reconvene Thurs 11am PT. :calendar:
